summary:
PYRO-SI is an intelligent scientific research and fire-safety decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of making decades of NASA microgravity combustion research easier to discover, compare, and interpret.

The platform organizes NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion investigations into an interactive research environment, featuring investigation ranking, evidence-based comparisons, flammability scenario exploration, and scientific research assistance. Its interactive 3D visualizations help users explore different space environments, including Earth orbit, lunar habitats, and Mars exploration scenarios.

By connecting experimental findings, atmospheric conditions, material flammability research, and fire-safety considerations, GODEYE aims to support researchers and engineers in understanding potential fire hazards in future crewed spacecraft and extraterrestrial habitats. It also explores how space combustion research can inform fire-safety technologies on Earth.
details:
What We Built

PYRO-SI is an interactive scientific intelligence platform designed to transform NASA's combustion research into accessible fire-safety insights for human space exploration.

The platform consists of five primary areas:

  1. GodEye Orbital & Habitat Visualization: Interactive 3D environments representing Earth orbit, lunar habitats, Mars habitats, and different gravitational conditions. It provides visual context for understanding combustion across space environments.
  2. NASA PSI Investigation Intelligence: A searchable investigation catalogue that organizes combustion experiments, their objectives, fuel types, experimental conditions, measurement techniques, and available research evidence. Users can rank and compare investigations based on their relevance to different fire-safety requirements.
  3. Flammability & Scenario Simulator: An interactive environment for exploring oxygen concentration, atmospheric pressure, airflow, gravity, and their relationships to material flammability. Model outputs are distinguished from experimentally measured results.
  4. Scientific Research Co-Pilot: An evidence-oriented research interface connecting combustion investigations, historical spacecraft fire incidents, relevant scientific publications, and potential terrestrial applications.
  5. Mission Safety Intelligence: A research and reporting interface that organizes relevant findings and communicates their implications for future spacecraft and habitat safety.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The platform aims to reduce the difficulty of navigating large scientific archives and help researchers identify relevant experiments, compare experimental conditions, explore fire-safety scenarios, and recognize gaps in existing research.

Its intended applications include spacecraft fire prevention, material selection, smoke detection research, suppression technologies, lunar habitat safety, and future Mars exploration.

Technologies Used

  • HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript
  • Three.js and WebGL for interactive 3D environments
  • HTML5 Canvas for scientific visualizations
  • JSON for structured research and investigation metadata
  • Python for data processing and validation scripts
  • Google Antigravity for AI-assisted development and multi-agent engineering workflows

Creativity and Innovation

Rather than presenting NASA combustion research as disconnected datasets, GODEYE // PYRO-SI brings investigation discovery, scientific comparison, interactive environmental visualization, and fire-safety scenario exploration together in one platform.

The project emphasizes scientific transparency by distinguishing measured, reported, derived, modelled, illustrative, and unknown information rather than presenting every result as experimentally proven.
